source: RFC 0007 §5.7 (DR1-E-2, RC review round 1 area E; designs confirmed by the maintainer's coordinator, 2026-11-23; DR2-E-2, RC review round 2 areas E to H)
statement: A new change of a document is refused once the document holds cosec.control.revisions.max-count open changes (50 by default), the revisions the operator keeps; the count is read before the write, so proposals counted at the same moment all pass, and a document holds at most max-count open changes plus those written at once: an open change pins its base against reclamation, so what the open changes pin stays within the retention. A proposal, an :apply or a rollback past the bound first abandons, to make room, its author's own oldest change whose checks failed (a DRAFT, which cannot be edited), and is otherwise refused 409 OPEN_LIMIT, naming the oldest open change in heldBy; nothing is stored. A change that can still move on is never abandoned for room, nor another author's, and a break-glass request is never held to the bound. A change that does not read counts as open. A document keeps at most max-count ended changes, too: the write that ends a change removes the oldest ended changes past the bound, record and listing, whatever their age (a removal that fails warns and reclamation removes it later), and the reclamation pass, under its lease, removes the ended changes older than cosec.control.revisions.min-age whose change published no revision still retained. Only a change the store listed when it ended is removed: one that ended under 8.0.0-beta.7 or earlier stays. A removed change reads as no change (404); a retained revision whose change is gone is still explained, and still names its change, author and approvers in its own provenance. A change record is written with at most the largest body a route reads plus the document cap (18 MB by default), its operations, findings, confirmations and escalations included; a record past it is not written, and the proposal or step is refused 422 (DR2-E-2). With a new change, a document's open change records weigh at most max-count times the document cap (400 MB by default): past it the new change is refused 409 OPEN_LIMIT as past the count, saying it is the bytes, the author's own oldest failed draft first making room; a record that does not read weighs a document's worth. The ended records are bounded by the product, max-count records at the record cap (900 MB by default), and never measured. The startup line states what one document stores at most and that it multiplies by the documents.
guards: control:OpenLimitTest#open changes past their bytes are refused OPEN_LIMIT, saying it is the bytes - DR2-E-2
control:OpenLimitTest#the author's own failed draft makes room for bytes too - DR2-E-2
control:ChangeRecordBudgetTest#a record past its cap is not written - DR2-E-2
control:ChangeRecordBudgetTest#a proposal whose record would pass the cap is refused, and nothing is stored - DR2-E-2
control:ChangeRecordBudgetTest#the largest operations and escalations leave a document's worth for the findings - DR2-E-2
control:ChangeRecordBudgetTest#the bounds are derived from max-count and the document cap - DR2-E-2
